situation:
You are the assistant manager at VOSS STREET BAKING COMPANY, a wholesale bakery in its third generation of family ownership. The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend how the bakery should set the prices it charges its sixty café and grocery accounts.

Those prices live in a handwritten ledger. Each account was quoted by handshake, some thirty years ago, and no rule was written down. A spreadsheet built from two years of delivery tickets shows the oldest accounts paying below what several items cost to make, while cafés added since pay well above.

The bakery could publish one price list for every account, telling each what changed and why. The oldest accounts would absorb a steep increase and would learn they had been paying differently from their neighbours. They kept ordering through the years the bakery lost money, and the drivers say they still send most of its new business.

The other course holds the handshake prices where they are and raises only the newer cafés, who already pay the most and can compare invoices with anyone they like. The owner (judge) wants your recommendation and how the bakery should explain the change to the accounts it affects.

You will present your recommendation to the owner (judge) in the owner's office. The owner (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the questions, the owner (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of owner of VOSS STREET BAKING COMPANY, a wholesale bakery in its third generation of family ownership.

Business background is the same as the situation above. The prices for sixty accounts sit in a handwritten ledger with no rule behind them, a spreadsheet built from two years of delivery tickets shows the oldest accounts paying below cost while newer cafés pay well above, and the drivers say the oldest accounts still send most of the bakery's new business.

You have asked the assistant manager (participant) to recommend how the bakery should set its wholesale prices, and how the change should be explained to the accounts it affects.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year after we do this, what do you expect to have changed?
What might this cost us later that it does not cost us now?
